articleBody:
Getting ready for a full interior renovation requires getting your logistics in order well before demolition begins. A smooth project comes down to clear scopes, early material decisions, and proper approvals.

- [ ] Written project scope — Detail exactly which rooms, fixtures, flooring, and finishes are included to prevent mid-project confusion.
- [ ] Preliminary renovation budget — Set a realistic financial boundary with built-in allowance reserves for unexpected interior repairs.
- [ ] Existing home sketches or floor plans — Help your contractor assess current traffic flow, room dimensions, and fixture locations.
- [ ] Long-lead finish and fixture selections — Order custom cabinetry, tile, and plumbing fixtures early to prevent installation standstills.
- [ ] Confirmed municipal permit responsibility — Verify in writing that your licensed contractor submits drawings and handles local building inspections.
- [ ] Temporary living arrangement plan — Decide early how your family will cook, shower, and manage daily routines around construction zones.
- [ ] Designated staging and storage space — Clear out the rooms being remodeled and identify a secure spot for delivered building materials.
- [ ] Written change-order agreement — Establish how unexpected field conditions or scope adjustments get documented and priced.

How to use this checklist:
Work through these items with your general contractor during your planning meetings. Preparing these details early keeps your timeline intact and minimizes disruption. To discuss your project and request a free quote, call Bay City Remodeling & Bathrooms at 813-362-0114.
